title: Oboza durian: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Oboza durian: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Oboza durian is a durian variety from Alfonso and Conchita Abad. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Oboza is a registered durian variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1997 as NSIC 1997 Dr 05. Alfonso and Conchita Abad bred it.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Oboza durian is grown

blocks.text: Compare it with the others in our [durian variety finder](/crop-varieties/durian), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Oboza was about 11 years old and about 10 meters tall when it was registered. It bears regularly, with fruit in June August. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
The pests and diseases that hit durian fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Oboza weighs about 2000 grams, and its shape is ellipsoid. The flesh is yellow and smooth and firm. Its sweetness measured 27 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 21.25 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is June August, bearing regular.
Where and when to plant Oboza durian

Davao growers plant named clones such as Puyat and Arancillo for their thick, creamy flesh and small seeds. Plant grafted trees of a known clone, and mix clones for better fruit set. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Oboza?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
